newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African platinum shares jump with surging metal.
newsitem.headline: S.African platinum shares jump with surging metal.

text.p: Shares in South African platinum mines leapt ahead on Wednesday, reacting to a surge in metal prices fuelled by a wildcat strike at Rustenburg Platinum Holdings Ltd, the world's biggest producer.

Rustenburg itself advanced 100 cents to 71.25 rands as investors ignored the negative impact of the illegal stoppage which has affected 15-20 percent of production at the mine and concentrated instead on the bullish price impact.
Potgietersrust Platinums Ltd jumped 120 cents to 28.20 rand while Lebowa Platinum Mines Ltd gained eight cents to 290.
"The shares are up on the back of the metal and because of the strike at Rustenburg," said one dealer, adding that the platinum position appeared particularly tight in Japan.
Platinum prices broke through the $400 mark on Wednesday to reach their highest levels since May 1996 and the metal was last trading at $404.75/405.75 an ounce.
Dealers said the Rustenburg strike came against a backdrop of an already tightening supply position due to lower shipments from Russia, the second largest supplier after South Africa.
Rustenburg produced 690,000 ounces of platinum in the six months to December 31, 1996, equivalent to around a quarter of world supply.
